ii_maes_compiles_and_runs.label: measured
ii_maes_compiles_and_runs.finding: A program using -maes DOES NOT COMPILE on this host. -maes is an x86-64-only option and clang rejects it outright for the arm64 target. Compilation with -march=armv8.6-a+crypto of x86-intrinsic code (wmmintrin.h) also fails. An arm64-native program using the ARMv8 crypto extension (vaeseq/vaesmcq) with -march=armv8.6-a+crypto DOES compile and the binary RUNS (returncode 0 on bench/selftest/vec) — but the v1..v4 benchmark programs all FAILED the FIPS-197 known-answer selftest and the openssl cross-check, so no accelerated throughput number from them is valid (see item iii).

value.maes_exact_reason: clang: error: unsupported option '-maes' for target 'arm64-apple-darwin25.6.0'
value.arm64_bench_correctness: INVALID — selftest match=NO against the FIPS-197 AES-128 KAT; 0/8 vectors agree with the openssl CLI (run2r-v4-verify.json). The correct composition of ARM AESE/AESMC was not established within this task's run budget.

iii_aes_ni_throughput.label: invalid_measurement
iii_aes_ni_throughput.finding: No valid hardware-AES throughput figure exists for this task. The measured host has no x86-64 AES-NI at all (item ii); the arm64 crypto-extension benchmark compiled and ran but produced ciphertexts that fail the FIPS-197 known-answer test and disagree with the openssl CLI on all 8 cross-check vectors (while the pure-Python implementation agrees 4/4, run3-python.json), so its throughput numbers are the throughput of a WRONG cipher and are classified invalid_measurement. They are preserved below for the record, NOT as usable figures, and none of them may be used to size any budget.

value.open_issue: the composition of ARM AESE (which applies SubBytes+ShiftRows+XOR roundkey) with AESMC (MixColumns) was never made to reproduce FIPS-197 within 4 program versions and 3 benchmark runs; a successor task with fresh run budget is required before ANY hardware-AES throughput may be quoted for budgeting on this host.

contradiction_resolution.record_a: ledger/questions/RQ-AES-001.yaml constraints: 'gcc 13.3.0 with -maes, python3 with pycryptodome 3.23.0, and the openssl CLI are available' (4 CPU cores, 15 GB RAM, no GPU, no sage)
contradiction_resolution.record_b: ledger/goals/GOAL-AES-001.yaml next_action: GF(2^8) census leg blocked because 'neither numpy nor a small C program is installed'
contradiction_resolution.finding: ON THE EXACT POINT OF DISAGREEMENT — whether a usable C toolchain with AES acceleration exists — the measurement SUPPORTS NEITHER RECORD AS WRITTEN, and resolves the contradiction against Record A on its specific claim: (1) a C compiler exists under the name gcc (supports the C-compiler-exists half of Record A against Record B); (2) it is NOT gcc 13.3.0 (Record A's version string is wrong on this host, measured: Apple clang 17.0.0, arm64-apple-darwin25.6.0); (3) -maes DOES NOT COMPILE, so Record A's 'with -maes ... available' is MEASURED FALSE on this host; (4) an arm64-native AES-accelerated compile-and-run path exists (-march=armv8.6-a+crypto, compiles, runs), but no correct (FIPS-197/openssl-agreeing) accelerated benchmark was produced within this task's run budget, so no accelerated throughput is available for budgeting; (5) Record B is MEASURED FALSE on its numpy half (numpy 2.4.4 importable, run1-inventory.json) and its C-compiler half (a C compiler exists), so the census-leg blocking premise as written is wrong on both named dependencies; (6) pycryptodome, which Record A lists as available, is MEASURED ABSENT (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'Crypto').
contradiction_resolution.on_what_the_receipt_is_silent: This receipt is SILENT on: whether the GOAL-AES-001 census leg is feasible (its memory/work profile was not measured here); on any hardware-AES throughput figure (invalid measurement, item iii); on multi-core scaling for any valid implementation (not measured); on everything about AES cryptanalysis at any round count (no cryptanalysis performed); on gcc 13.3.0/x86-64/AES-NI on any host other than the one measured (the host identity is recorded in run1-inventory.json: Darwin 25.6.0, Apple M4 Pro, Mac16,7).
contradiction_resolution.correction_of_record_status: This receipt is the correction of record. Neither RQ-AES-001 nor GOAL-AES-001 is edited; a successor Coordinator decision record is the proper channel for any ledger consequence.
